content.english: ℟. And my mouth shall declare thy praise.

content.english: ℣. O God, ✠ come to my assistance;

content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King of Apostles, * O come, let us adore.

content.latin: Ant. Regem Apostolórum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King of Apostles, * O come, let us adore.

content.latin: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Ant. Regem Apostolórum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King of Apostles, * O come, let us adore.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us adore.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

content.latin: Ant. Regem Apostolórum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King of Apostles, * O come, let us adore.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us adore.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King of Apostles, * O come, let us adore.

content.latin: Egrégie Doctor, Paule, mores ínstrue,
content.english: Our souls' great teacher, Paul, our guide in wisdom's ways,

content.latin: Et nostra tecum péctora in cælum trahe;
content.english: Teach us, our fainting hearts, to heaven's glad clime to raise,

content.latin: Veláta dum merídiem cernat fides,
content.english: Till faith in clearest light her bright meridian gains,

content.latin: Et solis instar sola regnet cáritas.
content.english: And love with sun-like fire within each bosom reigns.

content.latin: Sit Trinitáti sempitérna glória,
content.english: All honour, might, and power, and hymns of joy we bring,

content.latin: Honor, potéstas atque iubilátio,
content.english: While to the Trinity eternal praise we sing;

content.latin: In unitáte, quæ gubérnat ómnia,
content.english: He rules the universe in wondrous Unity,

content.latin: Per univérsa æternitátis sǽcula.
content.english: And shall, throughout the days of all eternity.

content.english: Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Qui operátus est * Petro in apostolátum, operátus est et mihi inter gentes: et cognovérunt grátiam, quæ data est mihi a Christo Dómino.
content.english: Ant. He That wrought effectually * in Peter to the Apostleship, the Same was mighty in me toward the Gentiles, and they perceived the grace that was given unto me of the Lord Christ.

content.latin: Psalmus 18 [1]
content.english: Psalm 18 [1]

content.latin: 18:2 Cæli enárrant glóriam Dei: * et ópera mánuum eius annúntiat firmaméntum.
content.english: 18:2 The heavens shew forth the glory of God, * and the firmament declareth the work of his hands.

content.latin: 18:3 Dies diéi erúctat verbum, * et nox nocti índicat sciéntiam.
content.english: 18:3 Day to day uttereth speech, * and night to night sheweth knowledge.

content.latin: 18:4 Non sunt loquélæ, neque sermónes, * quorum non audiántur voces eórum.
content.english: 18:4 There are no speeches nor languages, * where their voices are not heard.

content.latin: 18:5 In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum: * et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.
content.english: 18:5 Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth: * and their words unto the ends of the world.

content.latin: 18:6 In sole pósuit tabernáculum suum: * et ipse tamquam sponsus procédens de thálamo suo:
content.english: 18:6 He hath set his tabernacle in the sun: * and he, as a bridegroom coming out of his bride chamber,

content.latin: 18:6 Exsultávit ut gigas ad curréndam viam, * a summo cælo egréssio eius:
content.english: 18:6 Hath rejoiced as a giant to run the way: * his going out is from the end of heaven,

content.latin: 18:7 Et occúrsus eius usque ad summum eius: * nec est qui se abscóndat a calóre eius.
content.english: 18:7 And his circuit even to the end thereof: * and there is no one that can hide himself from his heat.

content.latin: 18:8 Lex Dómini immaculáta, convértens ánimas: * testimónium Dómini fidéle, sapiéntiam præstans párvulis.
content.english: 18:8 The law of the Lord is unspotted, converting souls: * the testimony of the Lord is faithful, giving wisdom to little ones.

content.latin: 18:9 Iustítiæ Dómini rectæ, lætificántes corda: * præcéptum Dómini lúcidum, illúminans óculos.
content.english: 18:9 The justices of the Lord are right, rejoicing hearts: * the commandment of the Lord is lightsome, enlightening the eyes.

content.latin: 18:10 Timor Dómini sanctus, pérmanens in sǽculum sǽculi: * iudícia Dómini vera, iustificáta in semetípsa.
content.english: 18:10 The fear of the Lord is holy, enduring for ever and ever: * the judgments of the Lord are true, justified in themselves.

content.latin: 18:11 Desiderabília super aurum et lápidem pretiósum multum: * et dulcióra super mel et favum.
content.english: 18:11 More to be desired than gold and many precious stones: * and sweeter than honey and the honeycomb.

content.latin: 18:12 Étenim servus tuus custódit ea, * in custodiéndis illis retribútio multa.
content.english: 18:12 For thy servant keepeth them, * and in keeping them there is a great reward.

content.latin: 18:13 Delícta quis intéllegit? ab occúltis meis munda me: * et ab aliénis parce servo tuo.
content.english: 18:13 Who can understand sins? from my secret ones cleanse me, O Lord: * and from those of others spare thy servant.

content.latin: 18:14 Si mei non fúerint domináti, tunc immaculátus ero: * et emundábor a delícto máximo.
content.english: 18:14 If they shall have no dominion over me, then shall I be without spot: * and I shall be cleansed from the greatest sin.

content.latin: 18:15 Et erunt ut compláceant elóquia oris mei: * et meditátio cordis mei in conspéctu tuo semper.
content.english: 18:15 And the words of my mouth shall be such as may please: * and the meditation of my heart always in thy sight.

content.latin: 18:15 Dómine, adiútor meus, * et redémptor meus.
content.english: 18:15 O Lord, my helper, * and my redeemer.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: Ant. I know Whom I have believed, * and am persuaded that He is able to keep that which I have committed unto Him against that day, as a righteous Judge.

content.latin: Psalmus 33 [2]
content.english: Psalm 33 [2]

content.latin: 33:2 Benedícam Dóminum in omni témpore: * semper laus eius in ore meo.
content.english: 33:2 I will bless the Lord at all times, * his praise shall be always in my mouth.

content.latin: 33:3 In Dómino laudábitur ánima mea: * áudiant mansuéti, et læténtur.
content.english: 33:3 In the Lord shall my soul be praised: * let the meek hear and rejoice.

content.latin: 33:4 Magnificáte Dóminum mecum: * et exaltémus nomen eius in idípsum.
content.english: 33:4 O magnify the Lord with me; * and let us extol his name together.

content.latin: 33:5 Exquisívi Dóminum, et exaudívit me: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus meis erípuit me.
content.english: 33:5 I sought the Lord, and he heard me; * and he delivered me from all my troubles.

content.latin: 33:6 Accédite ad eum, et illuminámini: * et fácies vestræ non confundéntur.
content.english: 33:6 Come ye to him and be enlightened: * and your faces shall not be confounded.

content.latin: 33:7 Iste pauper clamávit, et Dóminus exaudívit eum: * et de ómnibus tribulatiónibus eius salvávit eum.
content.english: 33:7 This poor man cried, and the Lord heard him: * and saved him out of all his troubles.

content.latin: 33:8 Immíttet Ángelus Dómini in circúitu timéntium eum: * et erípiet eos.
content.english: 33:8 The Angel of the Lord shall encamp round about them that fear him: * and shall deliver them.

content.latin: 33:9 Gustáte, et vidéte quóniam suávis est Dóminus: * beátus vir, qui sperat in eo.
content.english: 33:9 O taste, and see that the Lord is sweet: * blessed is the man that hopeth in him.

content.latin: 33:10 Timéte Dóminum, omnes sancti eius: * quóniam non est inópia timéntibus eum.
content.english: 33:10 Fear the Lord, all ye his saints: * for there is no want to them that fear him.

content.latin: 33:11 Dívites eguérunt et esuriérunt: * inquiréntes autem Dóminum non minuéntur omni bono.
content.english: 33:11 The rich have wanted, and have suffered hunger: * but they that seek the Lord shall not be deprived of any good.

content.latin: 33:12 Veníte, fílii, audíte me: * timórem Dómini docébo vos.
content.english: 33:12 Come, children, hearken to me: * I will teach you the fear of the Lord.

content.latin: 33:13 Quis est homo qui vult vitam: * díligit dies vidére bonos?
content.english: 33:13 Who is the man that desireth life: * who loveth to see good days?

content.latin: 33:14 Próhibe linguam tuam a malo: * et lábia tua ne loquántur dolum.
content.english: 33:14 Keep thy tongue from evil, * and thy lips from speaking guile.

content.latin: 33:15 Divérte a malo, et fac bonum: * inquíre pacem, et perséquere eam.
content.english: 33:15 Turn away from evil and do good: * seek after peace and pursue it.

content.latin: 33:16 Óculi Dómini super iustos: * et aures eius in preces eórum.
content.english: 33:16 The eyes of the Lord are upon the just: * and his ears unto their prayers.

content.latin: 33:17 Vultus autem Dómini super faciéntes mala: * ut perdat de terra memóriam eórum.
content.english: 33:17 But the countenance of the Lord is against them that do evil things: * to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth.

content.latin: 33:18 Clamavérunt iusti, et Dóminus exaudívit eos: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus eórum liberávit eos.
content.english: 33:18 The just cried, and the Lord heard them: * and delivered them out of all their troubles.

content.latin: 33:19 Iuxta est Dóminus iis, qui tribuláto sunt corde: * et húmiles spíritu salvábit.
content.english: 33:19 The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a contrite heart: * and he will save the humble of spirit.

content.latin: 33:20 Multæ tribulatiónes iustórum: * et de ómnibus his liberábit eos Dóminus.
content.english: 33:20 Many are the afflictions of the just; * but out of them all will the Lord deliver them.

content.latin: 33:21 Custódit Dóminus ómnia ossa eórum: * unum ex his non conterétur.
content.english: 33:21 The Lord keepeth all their bones, * not one of them shall be broken.

content.latin: 33:22 Mors peccatórum péssima: * et qui odérunt iustum, delínquent.
content.english: 33:22 The death of the wicked is very evil: * and they that hate the just shall be guilty.

content.latin: 33:23 Rédimet Dóminus ánimas servórum suórum: * et non delínquent omnes qui sperant in eo.
content.english: 33:23 The Lord will redeem the souls of his servants: * and none of them that trust in him shall offend.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.english: Ant. I know Whom I have believed, and am persuaded that He is able to keep that which I have committed unto Him against that day, as a righteous Judge.

content.english: Ant. To me to live is Christ, * and to die is gain: God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ.

content.latin: Psalmus 44 [3]
content.english: Psalm 44 [3]

content.latin: 44:2 Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: * dico ego ópera mea Regi.
content.english: 44:2 My heart hath uttered a good word; * I speak my works to the King.

content.latin: 44:2 Lingua mea cálamus scribæ: * velóciter scribéntis.
content.english: 44:2 My tongue is the pen of a scrivener * that writeth swiftly.

content.latin: 44:3 Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis: * proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.
content.english: 44:3 Thou art beautiful above the sons of men: grace is poured abroad in thy lips; * therefore hath God blessed thee for ever.

content.latin: 44:4 Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, * potentíssime.
content.english: 44:4 Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, * O thou most mighty.

content.latin: 44:5 Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua: * inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
content.english: 44:5 With thy comeliness and thy beauty * set out, proceed prosperously, and reign.

content.latin: 44:5 Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et iustítiam: * et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.
content.english: 44:5 Because of truth and meekness and justice: * and thy right hand shall conduct thee wonderfully.

content.latin: 44:6 Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ, pópuli sub te cadent: * in corda inimicórum Regis.
content.english: 44:6 Thy arrows are sharp: under thee shall people fall, * into the hearts of the king’s enemies.

content.latin: 44:7 Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum sǽculi: * virga directiónis virga regni tui.
content.english: 44:7 Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: * the sceptre of thy kingdom is a sceptre of uprightness.

content.latin: 44:8 Dilexísti iustítiam, et odísti iniquitátem: * proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ præ consórtibus tuis.
content.english: 44:8 Thou hast loved justice, and hated iniquity: * therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.

content.latin: 44:9 Myrrha, et gutta, et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a dómibus ebúrneis: * ex quibus delectavérunt te fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.
content.english: 44:9 Myrrh and stacte and cassia perfume thy garments, from the ivory houses: * out of which the daughters of kings have delighted thee in thy glory.

content.latin: 44:10 Ástitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto: * circúmdata varietáte.
content.english: 44:10 The queen stood on thy right hand, in gilded clothing; * surrounded with variety.

content.latin: 44:11 Audi fília, et vide, et inclína aurem tuam: * et oblivíscere pópulum tuum et domum patris tui.
content.english: 44:11 Hearken, O daughter, and see, and incline thy ear: * and forget thy people and thy father’s house.

content.latin: 44:12 Et concupíscet Rex decórem tuum: * quóniam ipse est Dóminus Deus tuus, et adorábunt eum.
content.english: 44:12 And the king shall greatly desire thy beauty; * for he is the Lord thy God, and him they shall adore.

content.latin: 44:13 Et fíliæ Tyri in munéribus * vultum tuum deprecabúntur: omnes dívites plebis.
content.english: 44:13 And the daughters of Tyre with gifts, * yea, all the rich among the people, shall entreat thy countenance.

content.latin: 44:14 Omnis glória eius fíliæ Regis ab intus, * in fímbriis áureis circumamícta varietátibus.
content.english: 44:14 All the glory of the king’s daughter is within, * in golden borders, clothed round about with varieties.

content.latin: 44:15 Adducéntur Regi vírgines post eam: * próximæ eius afferéntur tibi.
content.english: 44:15 After her shall virgins be brought to the king: * her neighbours shall be brought to thee.

content.latin: 44:16 Afferéntur in lætítia et exsultatióne: * adducéntur in templum Regis.
content.english: 44:16 They shall be brought with gladness and rejoicing: * they shall be brought into the temple of the king.

content.latin: 44:17 Pro pátribus tuis nati sunt tibi fílii: * constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram.
content.english: 44:17 Instead of thy fathers, sons are born to thee: * thou shalt make them princes over all the earth.

content.latin: 44:18 Mémores erunt nóminis tui: * in omni generatióne et generatiónem.
content.english: 44:18 They shall remember thy name * throughout all generations.

content.latin: 44:18 Proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum: * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 44:18 Therefore shall people praise thee for ever; yea, * for ever and ever.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Mihi vívere Christus est, et mori lucrum: gloriári me opórtet in cruce Dómini nostri Iesu Christi.
content.english: Ant. To me to live is Christ, and to die is gain: God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ.

content.latin: Ant. Tu es vas electiónis, * sancte Paule Apóstole, prædicátor veritátis in univérso mundo.
content.english: Ant. O Holy Apostle Paul, * thou art a chosen vessel unto God, to preach the Gospel throughout the whole world.

content.latin: Psalmus 46 [4]
content.english: Psalm 46 [4]

content.latin: 46:2 Omnes gentes, pláudite mánibus: * iubiláte Deo in voce exsultatiónis.
content.english: 46:2 O clap your hands, all ye nations: * shout unto God with the voice of joy,

content.latin: 46:3 Quóniam Dóminus excélsus, terríbilis: * Rex magnus super omnem terram.
content.english: 46:3 For the Lord is high, terrible: * a great king over all the earth.

content.latin: 46:4 Subiécit pópulos nobis: * et gentes sub pédibus nostris.
content.english: 46:4 He hath subdued the people under us; * and the nations under our feet.

content.latin: 46:5 Elégit nobis hereditátem suam: * spéciem Iacob, quam diléxit.
content.english: 46:5 He hath chosen for us his inheritance, * the beauty of Jacob which he hath loved.

content.latin: 46:6 Ascéndit Deus in iúbilo: * et Dóminus in voce tubæ.
content.english: 46:6 God is ascended with jubilee, * and the Lord with the sound of trumpet.

content.latin: 46:7 Psállite Deo nostro, psállite: * psállite Regi nostro, psállite.
content.english: 46:7 Sing praises to our God, sing ye: * sing praises to our king, sing ye.

content.latin: 46:8 Quóniam Rex omnis terræ Deus: * psállite sapiénter.
content.english: 46:8 For God is the king of all the earth: * sing ye wisely.

content.latin: 46:9 Regnábit Deus super gentes: * Deus sedet super sedem sanctam suam.
content.english: 46:9 God shall reign over the nations: * God sitteth on his holy throne.

content.latin: 46:10 Príncipes populórum congregáti sunt cum Deo Ábraham: * quóniam dii fortes terræ veheménter eleváti sunt.
content.english: 46:10 The princes of the people are gathered together, with the God of Abraham: * for the strong gods of the earth are exceedingly exalted.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Tu es vas electiónis, sancte Paule Apóstole, prædicátor veritátis in univérso mundo.
content.english: Ant. O Holy Apostle Paul, thou art a chosen vessel unto God, to preach the Gospel throughout the whole world.

content.latin: Ant. Magnus sanctus Paulus * vas electiónis, vere digne est glorificándus, qui et méruit thronum duodécimum possidére.
content.english: Ant. Paul is made one of the chiefest among the Saints, * and a chosen vessel; verily he is worthy to be glorified, for he was made worthy to sit upon one of the twelve thrones.

content.latin: Psalmus 60 [5]
content.english: Psalm 60 [5]

content.latin: 60:2 Exáudi, Deus, deprecatiónem meam: * inténde oratióni meæ.
content.english: 60:2 Hear, O God, my supplication: * be attentive to my prayer.

content.latin: 60:3 A fínibus terræ ad te clamávi: * dum anxiarétur cor meum, in petra exaltásti me.
content.english: 60:3 To thee have I cried from the ends of the earth: * when my heart was in anguish, thou hast exalted me on a rock.

content.latin: 60:4 Deduxísti me, quia factus es spes mea: * turris fortitúdinis a fácie inimíci.
content.english: 60:4 Thou hast conducted me; for thou hast been my hope: * a tower of strength against the face of the enemy.

content.latin: 60:5 Inhabitábo in tabernáculo tuo in sǽcula: * prótegar in velaménto alárum tuárum.
content.english: 60:5 In thy tabernacle I shall dwell for ever: * I shall be protected under the covert of thy wings.

content.latin: 60:6 Quóniam tu, Deus meus, exaudísti oratiónem meam: * dedísti hereditátem timéntibus nomen tuum.
content.english: 60:6 For thou, my God, hast heard my prayer: * thou hast given an inheritance to them that fear thy name.

content.latin: 60:7 Dies super dies regis adícies: * annos eius usque in diem generatiónis et generatiónis.
content.english: 60:7 Thou wilt add days to the days of the king: * his years even to generation and generation.

content.latin: 60:8 Pérmanet in ætérnum in conspéctu Dei: * misericórdiam et veritátem eius quis requíret?
content.english: 60:8 He abideth for ever in the sight of God: * his mercy and truth who shall search?

content.latin: 60:9 Sic psalmum dicam nómini tuo in sǽculum sǽculi: * ut reddam vota mea de die in diem.
content.english: 60:9 So will I sing a psalm to thy name for ever and ever: * that I may pay my vows from day to day.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.english: Ant. Paul is made one of the chiefest among the Saints, and a chosen vessel; verily he is worthy to be glorified, for he was made worthy to sit upon one of the twelve thrones.

content.latin: Ant. Bonum certámen * certávi, cursum consummávi, fidem servávi.
content.english: Ant. I have fought a good fight, * I have finished my course, I have kept the faith.

content.latin: Psalmus 63 [6]
content.english: Psalm 63 [6]

content.latin: 63:2 Exáudi, Deus, oratiónem meam cum déprecor: * a timóre inimíci éripe ánimam meam.
content.english: 63:2 Hear, O God, my prayer, when I make supplication to thee: * deliver my soul from the fear of the enemy.

content.latin: 63:3 Protexísti me a convéntu malignántium: * a multitúdine operántium iniquitátem.
content.english: 63:3 Thou hast protected me from the assembly of the malignant; * from the multitude of the workers of iniquity.

content.latin: 63:4 Quia exacuérunt ut gládium linguas suas: * intendérunt arcum rem amáram, ut sagíttent in occúltis immaculátum.
content.english: 63:4 For they have whetted their tongues like a sword; * they have bent their bow a bitter thing, to shoot in secret the undefiled.

content.latin: 63:6 Súbito sagittábunt eum, et non timébunt: * firmavérunt sibi sermónem nequam.
content.english: 63:6 They will shoot at him on a sudden, and will not fear: * they are resolute in wickedness.

content.latin: 63:6 Narravérunt ut abscónderent láqueos: * dixérunt: Quis vidébit eos?
content.english: 63:6 They have talked of hiding snares; * they have said: Who shall see them?

content.latin: 63:7 Scrutáti sunt iniquitátes: * defecérunt scrutántes scrutínio.
content.english: 63:7 They have searched after iniquities: * they have failed in their search.

content.latin: 63:7 Accédet homo ad cor altum: * et exaltábitur Deus.
content.english: 63:7 Man shall come to a deep heart: * and God shall be exalted.

content.latin: 63:8 Sagíttæ parvulórum factæ sunt plagæ eórum: * et infirmátæ sunt contra eos linguæ eórum.
content.english: 63:8 The arrows of children are their wounds: * and their tongues against them are made weak.

content.latin: 63:9 Conturbáti sunt omnes qui vidébant eos: * et tímuit omnis homo.
content.english: 63:9 All that saw them were troubled; * and every man was afraid.

content.latin: 63:10 Et annuntiavérunt ópera Dei, * et facta eius intellexérunt.
content.english: 63:10 And they declared the works of God: * and understood his doings.

content.latin: 63:11 Lætábitur iustus in Dómino, et sperábit in eo, * et laudabúntur omnes recti corde.
content.english: 63:11 The just shall rejoice in the Lord, and shall hope in him: * and all the upright in heart shall be praised.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Bonum certámen certávi, cursum consummávi, fidem servávi.
content.english: Ant. I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith.

content.latin: Ant. Saulus, qui et Paulus, * magnus prædicátor, a Deo confortátus convalescébat, et confundébat Iudǽos.
content.english: Ant. Saul, who also is called Paul, * was made a great preacher, and, being of God increased the more in strength, he confounded the Jews.

content.latin: Psalmus 74 [7]
content.english: Psalm 74 [7]

content.latin: 74:2 Confitébimur tibi, Deus: * confitébimur, et invocábimus nomen tuum.
content.english: 74:2 We will praise thee, O God: * we will praise, and we will call upon thy name.

content.latin: 74:3 Narrábimus mirabília tua: * cum accépero tempus, ego iustítias iudicábo.
content.english: 74:3 We will relate thy wondrous works: * when I shall take a time, I will judge justices.

content.latin: 74:4 Liquefácta est terra, et omnes qui hábitant in ea: * ego confirmávi colúmnas eius.
content.english: 74:4 The earth is melted, and all that dwell therein: * I have established the pillars thereof.

content.latin: 74:5 Dixi iníquis: Nolíte iníque ágere: * et delinquéntibus: Nolíte exaltáre cornu:
content.english: 74:5 I said to the wicked: Do not act wickedly: * and to the sinners: Lift not up the horn.

content.latin: 74:6 Nolíte extóllere in altum cornu vestrum: * nolíte loqui advérsus Deum iniquitátem.
content.english: 74:6 Lift not up your horn on high: * speak not iniquity against God.

content.latin: 74:7 Quia neque ab Oriénte, neque ab Occidénte, neque a desértis móntibus: * quóniam Deus iudex est.
content.english: 74:7 For neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the desert hills: * for God is the judge.

content.latin: 74:8 Hunc humíliat, et hunc exáltat: * quia calix in manu Dómini vini meri plenus misto.
content.english: 74:8 One he putteth down, and another he lifteth up: * for in the hand of the Lord there is a cup of strong wine full of mixture.

content.latin: 74:9 Et inclinávit ex hoc in hoc: verúmtamen fæx eius non est exinaníta: * bibent omnes peccatóres terræ.
content.english: 74:9 And he hath poured it out from this to that: but the dregs thereof are not emptied: * all the sinners of the earth shall drink.

content.latin: 74:10 Ego autem annuntiábo in sǽculum: * cantábo Deo Iacob.
content.english: 74:10 But I will declare for ever: * I will sing to the God of Jacob.

content.latin: 74:11 Et ómnia córnua peccatórum confríngam: * et exaltabúntur córnua iusti.
content.english: 74:11 And I will break all the horns of sinners: * but the horns of the just shall be exalted.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.english: Ant. Saul, who also is called Paul, was made a great preacher, and, being of God increased the more in strength, he confounded the Jews.

content.latin: Ant. Ne magnitúdo * revelatiónum extóllat me, datus est mihi stímulus carnis meæ, ángelus sátanæ, qui me colaphízet: propter quod ter Dóminum rogávi ut auferrétur a me, et dixit mihi Dóminus: Súfficit tibi, Paule, grátia mea.
content.english: Ant. Lest I should be exalted * above measure through the greatness of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me; for this thing I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me and the Lord said unto me: Paul, My grace is sufficient for thee.

content.latin: Psalmus 96 [8]
content.english: Psalm 96 [8]

content.latin: 96:1 Dóminus regnávit, exsúltet terra: * læténtur ínsulæ multæ.
content.english: 96:1 The Lord hath reigned, let the earth rejoice: * let many islands be glad.

content.latin: 96:2 Nubes, et calígo in circúitu eius: * iustítia, et iudícium corréctio sedis eius.
content.english: 96:2 Clouds and darkness are round about him: * justice and judgment are the establishment of his throne.

content.latin: 96:3 Ignis ante ipsum præcédet, * et inflammábit in circúitu inimícos eius.
content.english: 96:3 A fire shall go before him, * and shall burn his enemies round about.

content.latin: 96:4 Illuxérunt fúlgura eius orbi terræ: * vidit, et commóta est terra.
content.english: 96:4 His lightnings have shone forth to the world: * the earth saw and trembled.

content.latin: 96:5 Montes, sicut cera fluxérunt a fácie Dómini: * a fácie Dómini omnis terra.
content.english: 96:5 The mountains melted like wax, at the presence of the Lord: * at the presence of the Lord of all the earth.

content.latin: 96:6 Annuntiavérunt cæli iustítiam eius: * et vidérunt omnes pópuli glóriam eius.
content.english: 96:6 The heavens declared his justice: * and all people saw his glory.

content.latin: 96:7 Confundántur omnes, qui adórant sculptília: * et qui gloriántur in simulácris suis.
content.english: 96:7 Let them be all confounded that adore graven things, * and that glory in their idols.

content.latin: 96:7 Adoráte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * audívit, et lætáta est Sion.
content.english: 96:7 Adore him, all you his angels: * Sion heard, and was glad.

content.latin: 96:8 Et exsultavérunt fíliæ Iudæ, * propter iudícia tua, Dómine:
content.english: 96:8 And the daughters of Juda rejoiced, * because of thy judgments, O Lord.

content.latin: 96:9 Quóniam tu Dóminus Altíssimus super omnem terram: * nimis exaltátus es super omnes deos.
content.english: 96:9 For thou art the most high Lord over all the earth: * thou art exalted exceedingly above all gods.

content.latin: 96:10 Qui dilígitis Dóminum, odíte malum: * custódit Dóminus ánimas sanctórum suórum, de manu peccatóris liberábit eos.
content.english: 96:10 You that love the Lord, hate evil: * the Lord preserveth the souls of his saints, he will deliver them out of the hand of the sinner.

content.latin: 96:11 Lux orta est iusto, * et rectis corde lætítia.
content.english: 96:11 Light is risen to the just, * and joy to the right of heart.

content.latin: 96:12 Lætámini, iusti, in Dómino: * et confitémini memóriæ sanctificatiónis eius.
content.english: 96:12 Rejoice, ye just, in the Lord: * and give praise to the remembrance of his holiness.

content.english: Ant. There is laid up for me * a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous Judge, shall give me at that day.

content.latin: Psalmus 98 [9]
content.english: Psalm 98 [9]

content.latin: 98:1 Dóminus regnávit, irascántur pópuli: * qui sedet super Chérubim, moveátur terra.
content.english: 98:1 The Lord hath reigned, let the people be angry: * he that sitteth on the cherubims: let the earth be moved.

content.latin: 98:2 Dóminus in Sion magnus: * et excélsus super omnes pópulos.
content.english: 98:2 The Lord is great in Sion, * and high above all people.

content.latin: 98:3 Confiteántur nómini tuo magno: quóniam terríbile, et sanctum est: * et honor regis iudícium díligit.
content.english: 98:3 Let them give praise to thy great name: for it is terrible and holy: * and the king’s honour loveth judgment.

content.latin: 98:4 Tu parásti directiónes: * iudícium et iustítiam in Iacob tu fecísti.
content.english: 98:4 Thou hast prepared directions: * thou hast done judgment and justice in Jacob.

content.latin: 98:5 Exaltáte Dóminum, Deum nostrum, et adoráte scabéllum pedum eius: * quóniam sanctum est.
content.english: 98:5 Exalt ye the Lord our God, and adore his footstool, * for it is holy.

content.latin: 98:6 Móyses et Aaron in sacerdótibus eius: * et Sámuel inter eos, qui ínvocant nomen eius:
content.english: 98:6 Moses and Aaron among his priests: * and Samuel among them that call upon his name.

content.latin: 98:6 Invocábant Dóminum, et ipse exaudiébat eos: * in colúmna nubis loquebátur ad eos.
content.english: 98:6 They called upon the Lord, and he heard them: * he spoke to them in the pillar of the cloud.

content.latin: 98:7 Custodiébant testimónia eius, * et præcéptum quod dedit illis.
content.english: 98:7 They kept his testimonies, * and the commandment which he gave them.

content.latin: 98:8 Dómine, Deus noster, tu exaudiébas eos: * Deus, tu propítius fuísti eis, et ulcíscens in omnes adinventiónes eórum.
content.english: 98:8 Thou didst hear them, O Lord our God: * thou wast a merciful God to them, and taking vengeance on all their inventions.

content.latin: 98:9 Exaltáte Dóminum, Deum nostrum, et adoráte in monte sancto eius: * quóniam sanctus Dóminus, Deus noster.
content.english: 98:9 Exalt ye the Lord our God, and adore at his holy mountain: * for the Lord our God is holy.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: Ant. There is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous Judge, shall give me at that day.

content.latin: ℣. Nimis honoráti sunt amíci tui, Deus.
content.english: ℣. Thy friends, O Lord, are made exceedingly honourable.

content.latin: ℟. Nimis confortátus est principátus eórum.
content.english: ℟. Their principality is exceedingly strengthened.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

content.latin: Absolutio. Ipsíus píetas et misericórdia nos ádiuvet, qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivit et regnat in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Absolution. May His loving-kindness and mercy help us, Who liveth and reigneth with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

content.latin: Benedictio. Ille nos benedícat, qui sine fine vivit et regnat.
content.english: Benediction. May His blessing be upon us who doth live and reign for ever.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: De Actibus Apostolórum
content.english: Lesson from the Acts of the Apostles
Acts 13:1-4

content.latin: 1 Erant autem in Ecclésia quæ erat Antiochíæ, prophétæ et doctóres, in quibus Bárnabas et Simon, qui vocátur Niger, et Lucius Cyrenénsis et Mánahen, qui erat Heródis tetrárchæ collactáneus, et Saulus.
content.english: 1 Now there were in the church which was at Antioch, prophets and doctors, among whom was Barnabas, and Simon who was called Niger, and Lucius of Cyrene, and Manahen, who was the foster brother of Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.

content.latin: 2 Ministrántibus autem illis Dómino et ieiunántibus, dixit illis Spíritus Sanctus: Segregáte mihi Saulum et Bárnabam, in opus ad quod assúmpsi eos.
content.english: 2 And as they were ministering to the Lord, and fasting, the Holy Ghost said to them: Separate me Saul and Barnabas, for the work whereunto I have taken them.

content.latin: 3 Tunc ieiunántes et orántes imponentésque eis manus dimisérunt illos.
content.english: 3 Then they, fasting and praying, and imposing their hands upon them, sent them away.

content.latin: 4 Et ipsi quidem missi a Spíritu Sancto abiérunt Seleucíam et inde navigavérunt Cyprum.
content.english: 4 So they being sent by the Holy Ghost, went to Seleucia: and from thence they sailed to Cyprus.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℟. Qui operátus est Petro in apostolátum, operátus est et mihi inter gentes:
content.english: ℟. He That wrought effectually in Peter to the Apostleship, the Same was mighty in me toward the Gentiles,

content.latin: * Et cognovérunt grátiam Dei, quæ data est mihi.
content.english: * And they perceived the grace that was given unto me of the Lord Christ.

content.latin: ℣. Grátia Dei in me vácua non fuit, sed grátia eius semper in me manet.
content.english: ℣. The grace of God which was bestowed upon me was not in vain, but His grace abideth ever in me.

content.latin: ℟. Et cognovérunt grátiam Dei, quæ data est mihi.
content.english: ℟. And they perceived the grace that was given unto me of the Lord Christ.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

content.latin: Benedictio. Cuius festum cólimus, ipse intercédat pro nobis ad Dóminum.
content.english: Benediction. He whose feast-day we are keeping, be our Advocate with God.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.
Acts 13:5-8

content.latin: 5 Et, cum veníssent Salamínam, prædicábant verbum Dei in synagógis Iudæórum; habébant autem et Ioánnem in ministério.
content.english: 5 And when they were come to Salamina, they preached the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews. And they had John also in the ministry.

content.latin: 6 Et, cum perambulássent univérsam ínsulam usque Paphum, invenérunt quemdam virum magum pseudoprophétam Iudǽum, cui nomen erat Bariésu,
content.english: 6 And when they had gone through the whole island, as far as Paphos, they found a certain man, a magician, a false prophet, a Jew, whose name was Bar-jesu:

content.latin: 7 Qui erat cum procónsule Sérgio Paulo, viro prudénte. Hic, accersítis Bárnaba et Saulo, desiderábat audíre verbum Dei.
content.english: 7 Who was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, a prudent man. He sending for Barnabas and Saul, desired to hear the word of God.

content.latin: 8 Resistébat autem illis Elymas magus (sic enim interpretátur nomen eius) quærens avértere procónsulem a fide.
content.english: 8 But Elymas the magician (for so his name is interpreted) withstood them, seeking to turn away the proconsul from the faith.

content.latin: 9 Saulus autem, qui et Paulus, replétus Spíritu Sancto, íntuens in eum,
content.english: 9 Then Saul, otherwise Paul, filled with the Holy Ghost, looking upon him,

content.latin: 10 Dixit: O plene omni dolo et omni fallácia, fili diáboli, inimíce omnis iustítiæ, non désinis subvértere vias Dómini rectas?
content.english: 10 Said: O full of all guile, and of all deceit, child of the devil, enemy of all justice, thou ceasest not to pervert the right ways of the Lord.

content.latin: Apóstolus Paulus, quem certe invénimus sine ullis méritis bonis, immo cum multis méritis malis, Dei grátiam consecútum, reddéntis bona pro malis, videámus quid dicat, sua iam propinquánte passióne, scribens ad Timótheum: Ego enim iam ímmolor, inquit, et tempus resolutiónis meæ instat. Bonum certámen certávi, cursum consummávi, fidem servávi. Ista útique iam mérita sua bona commémorat; ut post bona mérita consequátur corónam, qui post mérita mala consecútus est grátiam. Dénique atténdite quid sequátur: Súperest, inquit, mihi coróna iustítiæ, quam reddet mihi Dóminus in illa die iustus iudex. Cui rédderet corónam iustus iudex, si non donásset grátiam miséricors Pater? Et quómodo esset ista coróna iustítiæ, nisi præcessísset grátia, quæ iustíficat ímpium? Quómodo ista débita redderétur, nisi prius illa gratúita donarétur?
content.english: The Apostle Paul was a man, who, when we first hear of him, had not only no merits, but a great many demerits. That man received the grace of God, Who returneth good for evil, and let us see in what sort of language, when the hour of his last sufferings was at hand, he wrote to Timothy. He saith: I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand. I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith. 2 Tim. iii. 6. Here he counteth his merits, whereon a crown was immediately to follow, just as grace had followed immediately on his demerits. Listen to what cometh next: Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous Judge, shall give me at that day. Unto whom would the Lord give a crown as a righteous Judge, if He had not first given grace, as a merciful Father? And how would that crown be a crown of righteousness, if there had not first come grace which justifieth the ungodly? How could a reward have been earned unless the power to earn had first been given unearned?

content.latin: 3:74 Benedícite, Ananía, Azaría, Mísaël, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:74 O Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, bless ye the Lord: * praise and exalt him above all for ever.

content.latin: 3:75 (Fit reverentia:) Benedicámus Patrem et Fílium cum Sancto Spíritu: * laudémus et superexaltémus eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:75 (Bow head) Let us bless the Father and the Son, with the Holy Ghost; * let us praise and exalt him above all for ever.

content.latin: 3:56 Benedíctus es, Dómine, in firmaménto cæli: * et laudábilis, et gloriósus, et superexaltátus in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:56 Blessed art thou, O Lord, in the firmament of heaven: * and worthy of praise, and glorious for ever.

content.latin: Ant. Damásci, præpósitus gentis Arétæ regis vóluit me comprehéndere: a frátribus per murum demíssus sum in sporta, et sic evási manus eius in nómine Dómini.
content.english: Ant. In Damascus the governor under Aretas the king was desirous to apprehend me; by the brethren in a basket was I let down by the wall, and so escaped I his hands, in the name of the Lord.

content.latin: Ant. Ter virgis cæsus sum, * semel lapidátus sum, ter naufrágium pértuli pro Christi nómine.
content.english: Ant. Thrice was I beaten with rods, * once was I stoned, thrice I suffered shipwreck, for Christ's name's sake.

content.latin: Psalmus 148 [5]
content.english: Psalm 148 [5]

content.latin: 148:1 Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.
content.english: 148:1 Praise ye the Lord from the heavens * praise ye him in the high places.

content.latin: 148:2 Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes eius.
content.english: 148:2 Praise ye him, all his angels: * praise ye him, all his hosts.

content.latin: 148:3 Laudáte eum, sol et luna: * laudáte eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.
content.english: 148:3 Praise ye him, O sun and moon: * praise him, all ye stars and light.

content.latin: 148:4 Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.
content.english: 148:4 Praise him, ye heavens of heavens: * and let all the waters that are above the heavens, praise the name of the Lord.

content.latin: 148:5 Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.
content.english: 148:5 For he spoke, and they were made: * he commanded, and they were created.

content.latin: 148:6 Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.
content.english: 148:6 He hath established them for ever, and for ages of ages: * he hath made a decree, and it shall not pass away.

content.latin: 148:7 Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.
content.english: 148:7 Praise the Lord from the earth, * ye dragons, and all ye deeps:

content.latin: 148:8 Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum: * quæ fáciunt verbum eius:
content.english: 148:8 Fire, hail, snow, ice, stormy winds * which fulfill his word:

content.latin: 148:9 Montes, et omnes colles: * ligna fructífera, et omnes cedri.
content.english: 148:9 Mountains and all hills, * fruitful trees and all cedars:

content.latin: 148:10 Béstiæ, et univérsa pécora: * serpéntes, et vólucres pennátæ:
content.english: 148:10 Beasts and all cattle: * serpents and feathered fowls:

content.latin: 148:11 Reges terræ, et omnes pópuli: * príncipes, et omnes iúdices terræ.
content.english: 148:11 Kings of the earth and all people: * princes and all judges of the earth:

content.latin: 148:12 Iúvenes, et vírgines: senes cum iunióribus laudent nomen Dómini: * quia exaltátum est nomen eius solíus.
content.english: 148:12 Young men and maidens: let the old with the younger, praise the name of the Lord: * For his name alone is exalted.

content.latin: 148:14 Conféssio eius super cælum et terram: * et exaltávit cornu pópuli sui.
content.english: 148:14 The praise of him is above heaven and earth: * and he hath exalted the horn of his people.

content.latin: 148:14 Hymnus ómnibus sanctis eius: * fíliis Israël, pópulo appropinquánti sibi.
content.english: 148:14 A hymn to all his saints: to the children of Israel, a people approaching him.

content.english: Ant. Thrice was I beaten with rods, once was I stoned, thrice I suffered shipwreck, for Christ's name's sake.

content.latin: Bonum certámen certávi, cursum consummávi, fidem servávi. In réliquo repósita est mihi coróna iustítiæ, quam reddet mihi Dóminus in illa die iustus iudex.
content.english: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith. Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous Judge, shall give me at that day.

content.latin: Exsúltet orbis gáudiis:
content.english: Now let the earth with joy resound,

content.latin: Cælum resúltet láudibus:
content.english: And heaven the chant re-echo round;

content.latin: Apostolórum glóriam
content.english: Nor heaven nor earth too high can raise

content.latin: Tellus et astra cóncinunt.
content.english: The great Apostles' glorious praise.

content.latin: Vos sæculórum iúdices,
content.english: O ye who, throned in glory dread,

content.latin: Et vera mundi lúmina:
content.english: Shall judge the living and the dead,

content.latin: Votis precámur córdium,
content.english: Lights of the world forevermore!

content.latin: Audíte voces súpplicum.
content.english: To you the suppliant prayer we pour.

content.latin: Qui templa cæli cláuditis,
content.english: Ye close the sacred gates on high;

content.latin: Serásque verbo sólvitis,
content.english: At your command apart they fly:

content.latin: Nos a reátu nóxios
content.english: Oh! loose for us the guilty chain

content.latin: Solvi iubéte, quǽsumus.
content.english: We strive to break, and strive in vain.

content.latin: Præcépta quorum prótinus
content.english: Sickness and health your voice obey;

content.latin: Languor salúsque séntiunt:
content.english: At your command they go or stay:

content.latin: Sanáte mentes lánguidas:
content.english: From sin's disease our souls restore;

content.latin: Augéte nos virtútibus.
content.english: In good confirm us more and more.

content.latin: Ut, cum redíbit árbiter
content.english: So when the world is at its end,

content.latin: In fine Christus sǽculi,
content.english: And Christ to judgement shall descend,

content.latin: Nos sempitérni gáudii
content.english: May we be called those joys to see

content.latin: Concédat esse cómpotes.
content.english: Prepared from all eternity.

content.latin: Patri, simúlque Fílio,
content.english: Praise to the Father, with the Son,

content.latin: Tibíque Sancte Spíritus,
content.english: And Holy Spirit, Three in One;

content.latin: Sicut fuit, sit iúgiter
content.english: As ever was in ages past,

content.latin: Sæclum per omne glória.
content.english: And so shall be while ages last.

content.english: ℣. O Holy Apostle Paul, thou art a chosen vessel unto God.

content.english: ℟. To preach the Gospel throughout the whole world.

content.english: Ant. Thus saith the Lord: * Ye, which have followed Me, shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

content.english: Canticle of Zacharias

content.latin: 1:68 Benedíctus ✠ Dóminus, Deus Israël: * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:
content.english: 1:68 Blessed be the Lord ✠ God of Israel; * because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people:

content.latin: 1:69 Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.
content.english: 1:69 And hath raised up an horn of salvation to us, * in the house of David his servant:

content.latin: 1:70 Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:
content.english: 1:70 As he spoke by the mouth of his holy Prophets, * who are from the beginning:

content.latin: 1:71 Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.
content.english: 1:71 Salvation from our enemies, * and from the hand of all that hate us:

content.latin: 1:72 Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.
content.english: 1:72 To perform mercy to our fathers, * and to remember his holy testament,

content.latin: 1:73 Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:
content.english: 1:73 The oath, which he swore to Abraham our father, * that he would grant to us,

content.latin: 1:74 Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.
content.english: 1:74 That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, * we may serve him without fear,

content.latin: 1:75 In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.
content.english: 1:75 In holiness and justice before him, * all our days.

content.latin: 1:76 Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:
content.english: 1:76 And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: * for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways:

content.latin: 1:77 Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:
content.english: 1:77 To give knowledge of salvation to his people, * unto the remission of their sins:

content.latin: 1:78 Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri: * in quibus visitávit nos, óriens ex alto:
content.english: 1:78 Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, * in which the Orient from on high hath visited us:

content.latin: 1:79 Illumináre his, qui in ténebris, et in umbra mortis sedent: * ad dirigéndos pedes nostros in viam pacis.
content.english: 1:79 To enlighten them that sit in darkness, and in the shadow of death: * to direct our feet into the way of peace.

content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Deus, qui multitúdinem géntium beáti Pauli Apóstoli prædicatióne docuísti: da nobis, quǽsumus; ut, cuius natalícia cólimus, eius apud te patrocínia sentiámus.
content.english: O God, Who, through the preaching of the Blessed Apostle Paul, hast caused the light of the Gospel to shine gloriously among the Gentiles, we beseech thee that we who keep the Feast of his birth, may, now that he is with thee, feel to our comfort that his prayer availeth much with thee.

content.latin: Commemoratio S. Petri Apostoli
content.english: Commemoration of St. Peter the Apostle

content.latin: Deus, qui beáto Petro Apóstolo tuo, collátis clávibus regni cæléstis, ligándi atque solvéndi pontifícium tradidísti: concéde; ut, intercessiónis eius auxílio, a peccatórum nostrórum néxibus liberémur:
content.english: O God, Who hast given unto thy Blessed Apostle Peter the keys of the kingdom of heaven, and the power to bind and to loose, loose us, we beseech thee, at his mighty intercession, from all the bands of our sins.

content.latin: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre, in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Who livest and reignest with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, world without end.

content.english: Now in the sun's new dawning ray,

content.english: Lowly of heart, our God we pray

content.latin: Ut in diúrnis áctibus
content.english: That he from harm may keep us free

content.latin: Nos servet a nocéntibus.
content.english: In all the deeds this day shall see.

content.latin: Linguam refrénans témperet,
content.english: May fear of him our tongues restrain,

content.latin: Ne litis horror ínsonet:
content.english: Lest strife unguarded speech should stain:

content.latin: Visum fovéndo cóntegat,
content.english: His favouring care our guardian be,

content.latin: Ne vanitátes háuriat.
content.english: Lest our eyes feed on vanity.

content.latin: Sint pura cordis íntima,
content.english: May every heart be pure from sin

content.latin: Absístat et vecórdia;
content.english: And folly find no place therein:

content.latin: Carnis terat supérbiam
content.english: Scant need of food, excess denied,

content.latin: Potus cibíque párcitas.
content.english: Wear down in us the body's pride.

content.latin: Ut, cum dies abscésserit,
content.english: That when the light of day is gone,

content.latin: Noctémque sors redúxerit,
content.english: And night in course shall follow on.

content.latin: Mundi per abstinéntiam
content.english: We, free from cares the world affords,

content.latin: Ipsi canámus glóriam.
content.english: May chant the praise that is our Lord's.

content.latin: Deo Patri sit glória,
content.english: All laud to God the Father be,

content.latin: Eiúsque soli Fílio,
content.english: All praise, Eternal Son, to thee:

content.latin: Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
content.english: All glory, as is ever meet,

content.latin: Nunc et per omne sǽculum.
content.english: To God the holy Paraclete.

content.english: Ant. In thee, O my God, * I put my trust; let me not be ashamed.

content.latin: Psalmus 24(1-7) [1]
24:1 Ad te, Dómine, levávi ánimam meam: * Deus meus, in te confído, non erubéscam.
content.english: 24:1 To thee, O Lord, have I lifted up my soul: * In thee, O my God, I put my trust; let me not be ashamed.

content.latin: 24:3 Neque irrídeant me inimíci mei: * étenim univérsi, qui sústinent te, non confundéntur.
content.english: 24:3 Neither let my enemies laugh at me: * for none of them that wait on thee shall be confounded.

content.latin: 24:4 Confundántur omnes iníqua agéntes * supervácue.
content.english: 24:4 Let all them be confounded that act unjust things * without cause.

content.latin: 24:4 Vias tuas, Dómine, demónstra mihi: * et sémitas tuas édoce me.
content.english: 24:4 Shew, O Lord, thy ways to me, * and teach me thy paths.

content.latin: 24:5 Dírige me in veritáte tua, et doce me: * quia tu es, Deus, salvátor meus, et te sustínui tota die.
content.english: 24:5 Direct me in thy truth, and teach me; * for thou art God my Saviour; and on thee have I waited all the day long.

content.latin: 24:6 Reminíscere miseratiónum tuárum, Dómine, * et misericordiárum tuárum, quæ a sǽculo sunt.
content.english: 24:6 Remember, O Lord, thy bowels of compassion; * and thy mercies that are from the beginning of the world.

content.latin: 24:7 Delícta iuventútis meæ, * et ignorántias meas ne memíneris.
content.english: 24:7 The sins of my youth * and my ignorances do not remember.

content.latin: 24:7 Secúndum misericórdiam tuam meménto mei tu: * propter bonitátem tuam, Dómine.
content.english: 24:7 According to thy mercy remember thou me: * for thy goodness’ sake, O Lord.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: 24:8 Dulcis et rectus Dóminus: * propter hoc legem dabit delinquéntibus in via.
content.english: 24:8 The Lord is sweet and righteous: * therefore he will give a law to sinners in the way.

content.latin: 24:9 Díriget mansuétos in iudício: * docébit mites vias suas.
content.english: 24:9 He will guide the mild in judgment: * he will teach the meek his ways.

content.latin: 24:10 Univérsæ viæ Dómini, misericórdia et véritas, * requiréntibus testaméntum eius et testimónia eius.
content.english: 24:10 All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth, * to them that seek after his covenant and his testimonies.

content.latin: 24:11 Propter nomen tuum, Dómine, propitiáberis peccáto meo: * multum est enim.
content.english: 24:11 For thy name’s sake, O Lord, thou wilt pardon my sin: * for it is great.

content.latin: 24:12 Quis est homo qui timet Dóminum? * legem státuit ei in via, quam elégit.
content.english: 24:12 Who is the man that feareth the Lord? * He hath appointed him a law in the way he hath chosen.

content.latin: 24:13 Ánima eius in bonis demorábitur: * et semen eius hereditábit terram.
content.english: 24:13 His soul shall dwell in good things: * and his seed shall inherit the land.

content.latin: 24:14 Firmaméntum est Dóminus timéntibus eum: * et testaméntum ipsíus ut manifestétur illis.
content.english: 24:14 The Lord is a firmament to them that fear him: * and his covenant shall be made manifest to them.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: 24:15 Óculi mei semper ad Dóminum: * quóniam ipse evéllet de láqueo pedes meos.
content.english: 24:15 My eyes are ever towards the Lord: * for he shall pluck my feet out of the snare.

content.latin: 24:16 Réspice in me, et miserére mei: * quia únicus et pauper sum ego.
content.english: 24:16 Look thou upon me, and have mercy on me; * for I am alone and poor.

content.latin: 24:17 Tribulatiónes cordis mei multiplicátæ sunt: * de necessitátibus meis érue me.
content.english: 24:17 The troubles of my heart are multiplied: * deliver me from my necessities.

content.latin: 24:18 Vide humilitátem meam, et labórem meum: * et dimítte univérsa delícta mea.
content.english: 24:18 See my abjection and my labour; * and forgive me all my sins.

content.latin: 24:19 Réspice inimícos meos quóniam multiplicáti sunt, * et ódio iníquo odérunt me.
content.english: 24:19 Consider my enemies for they are multiplied, * and have hated me with an unjust hatred.

content.latin: 24:20 Custódi ánimam meam, et érue me: * non erubéscam quóniam sperávi in te.
content.english: 24:20 Keep thou my soul, and deliver me: * I shall not be ashamed, for I have hoped in thee.

content.latin: 24:21 Innocéntes et recti adhæsérunt mihi: * quia sustínui te.
content.english: 24:21 The innocent and the upright have adhered to me: * because I have waited on thee.

content.latin: 24:22 Líbera, Deus, Israël, * ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus suis.
content.english: 24:22 Deliver Israel, O God, * from all his tribulations.

content.english: Psalm 40 [1]

content.latin: 40:2 Beátus qui intéllegit super egénum, et páuperem: * in die mala liberábit eum Dóminus.
content.english: 40:2 Blessed is he that understandeth concerning the needy and the poor: * the Lord will deliver him in the evil day.

content.latin: 40:3 Dóminus consérvet eum, et vivíficet eum, et beátum fáciat eum in terra: * et non tradat eum in ánimam inimicórum eius.
content.english: 40:3 The Lord preserve him and give him life, and make him blessed upon the earth: * and deliver him not up to the will of his enemies.

content.latin: 40:4 Dóminus opem ferat illi super lectum dolóris eius: * univérsum stratum eius versásti in infirmitáte eius.
content.english: 40:4 The Lord help him on his bed of sorrow: * thou hast turned all his couch in his sickness.

content.latin: 40:5 Ego dixi: Dómine, miserére mei: * sana ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi.
content.english: 40:5 I said: O Lord, be thou merciful to me: * heal my soul, for I have sinned against thee.

content.latin: 40:6 Inimíci mei dixérunt mala mihi: * Quando moriétur, et períbit nomen eius?
content.english: 40:6 My enemies have spoken evils against me: * when shall he die and his name perish?

content.latin: 40:7 Et si ingrediebátur ut vidéret, vana loquebátur: * cor eius congregávit iniquitátem sibi.
content.english: 40:7 And if he came in to see me, he spoke vain things: * his heart gathered together iniquity to itself.

content.latin: 40:7 Egrediebátur foras, * et loquebátur in idípsum.
content.english: 40:7 He went out * and spoke to the same purpose.

content.latin: 40:8 Advérsum me susurrábant omnes inimíci mei: * advérsum me cogitábant mala mihi.
content.english: 40:8 All my enemies whispered together against me: * they devised evils to me.

content.latin: 40:9 Verbum iníquum constituérunt advérsum me: * Numquid qui dormit non adíciet ut resúrgat?
content.english: 40:9 They determined against me an unjust word: * shall he that sleepeth rise again no more?

content.latin: 40:10 Étenim homo pacis meæ, in quo sperávi: * qui edébat panes meos, magnificávit super me supplantatiónem.
content.english: 40:10 For even the man of my peace, in whom I trusted, * who ate my bread, hath greatly supplanted me.

content.latin: 40:11 Tu autem, Dómine, miserére mei, et resúscita me: * et retríbuam eis.
content.english: 40:11 But thou, O Lord, have mercy on me, and raise me up again: * and I will requite them.

content.latin: 40:12 In hoc cognóvi quóniam voluísti me: * quóniam non gaudébit inimícus meus super me.
content.english: 40:12 By this I know, that thou hast had a good will for me: * because my enemy shall not rejoice over me.

content.latin: 40:13 Me autem propter innocéntiam suscepísti: * et confirmásti me in conspéctu tuo in ætérnum.
content.english: 40:13 But thou hast upheld me by reason of my innocence: * and hast established me in thy sight for ever.

content.latin: 40:14 Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum: * fiat, fiat.
content.english: 40:14 Blessed be the Lord the God of Israel from eternity to eternity. * So be it. So be it.

content.latin: Psalmus 41(2-6) [2]
41:2 Quemádmodum desíderat cervus ad fontes aquárum: * ita desíderat ánima mea ad te, Deus.
content.english: 41:2 As the hart panteth after the fountains of water; * so my soul panteth after thee, O God.

content.latin: 41:3 Sitívit ánima mea ad Deum fortem vivum: * quando véniam, et apparébo ante fáciem Dei?
content.english: 41:3 My soul hath thirsted after the strong living God; * when shall I come and appear before the face of God?

content.latin: 41:4 Fuérunt mihi lácrimæ meæ panes die ac nocte: * dum dícitur mihi cotídie: Ubi est Deus tuus?
content.english: 41:4 My tears have been my bread day and night, * whilst it is said to me daily: Where is thy God?

content.latin: 41:5 Hæc recordátus sum, et effúdi in me ánimam meam: * quóniam transíbo in locum tabernáculi admirábilis, usque ad domum Dei.
content.english: 41:5 These things I remembered, and poured out my soul in me: * for I shall go over into the place of the wonderful tabernacle, even to the house of God:

content.latin: 41:5 In voce exsultatiónis, et confessiónis: * sonus epulántis.
content.english: 41:5 With the voice of joy and praise; * the noise of one feasting.

content.latin: 41:6 Quare tristis es, ánima mea? * et quare contúrbas me?
content.english: 41:6 Why art thou sad, O my soul? * and why dost thou trouble me?

content.latin: 41:6 Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
content.english: 41:6 Hope in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

content.latin: 41:7 Ad meípsum ánima mea conturbáta est: * proptérea memor ero tui de terra Iordánis, et Hermóniim a monte módico.
content.english: 41:7 My soul is troubled within myself: * therefore will I remember thee from the land of Jordan and Hermoniim, from the little hill.

content.latin: 41:8 Abýssus abýssum ínvocat, * in voce cataractárum tuárum.
content.english: 41:8 Deep calleth on deep, * at the noise of thy flood-gates.

content.latin: 41:8 Ómnia excélsa tua, et fluctus tui * super me transiérunt.
content.english: 41:8 All thy heights and thy billows * have passed over me.

content.latin: 41:9 In die mandávit Dóminus misericórdiam suam: * et nocte cánticum eius.
content.english: 41:9 In the daytime the Lord hath commanded his mercy; * and a canticle to him in the night.

content.latin: 41:9 Apud me orátio Deo vitæ meæ, * dicam Deo: Suscéptor meus es.
content.english: 41:9 With me is prayer to the God of my life. * I will say to God: Thou art my support.

content.latin: 41:10 Quare oblítus es mei? * et quare contristátus incédo, dum afflígit me inimícus?
content.english: 41:10 Why hast thou forgotten me? * and why go I mourning, whilst my enemy afflicteth me?

content.latin: 41:11 Dum confringúntur ossa mea, * exprobravérunt mihi qui tríbulant me inimíci mei.
content.english: 41:11 Whilst my bones are broken, * my enemies who trouble me have reproached me;

content.latin: 41:11 Dum dicunt mihi per síngulos dies: Ubi est Deus tuus? * quare tristis es, ánima mea? et quare contúrbas me?
content.english: 41:11 Whilst they say to me day by day: Where is thy God? * Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why dost thou disquiet me?

content.latin: 41:12 Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
content.english: 41:12 Hope thou in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

content.latin: Ne magnitúdo revelatiónum extóllat me, datus est mihi stímulus carnis meæ, ángelus sátanæ, qui me colaphízet: propter quod ter Dóminum rogávi ut discéderet a me, et dixit mihi: Súfficit tibi grátia mea.
content.english: Lest I should be exalted above measure through the greatness of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan, to buffet me for this thing I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me and the Lord said unto me Paul, My grace is sufficient for thee.

content.latin: Deus, qui multitúdinem géntium beáti Pauli Apóstoli prædicatióne docuísti: da nobis, quǽsumus; ut, cuius natalícia cólimus, eius apud te patrocínia sentiámus.
content.english: O God, Who, through the preaching of the Blessed Apostle Paul, hast caused the light of the Gospel to shine gloriously among the Gentiles, we beseech thee that we who keep the Feast of his birth, may, now that he is with thee, feel to our comfort that his prayer availeth much with thee.

content.latin: Psalmus 43(2-9) [1]
43:2 Deus áuribus nostris audívimus: * patres nostri annuntiavérunt nobis.
content.english: 43:2 We have heard, O God, with our ears: * our fathers have declared to us,

content.latin: 43:2 Opus, quod operátus es in diébus eórum, * et in diébus antíquis.
content.english: 43:2 The work thou hast wrought in their days, * and in the days of old.

content.latin: 43:3 Manus tua gentes dispérdidit, et plantásti eos: * afflixísti pópulos, et expulísti eos.
content.english: 43:3 Thy hand destroyed the Gentiles, and thou plantedst them: * thou didst afflict the people and cast them out.

content.latin: 43:4 Nec enim in gládio suo possedérunt terram, * et brácchium eórum non salvávit eos:
content.english: 43:4 For they got not the possession of the land by their own sword: * neither did their own arm save them.

content.latin: 43:4 Sed déxtera tua, et brácchium tuum, et illuminátio vultus tui: * quóniam complacuísti in eis.
content.english: 43:4 But thy right hand and thy arm, and the light of thy countenance: * because thou wast pleased with them.

content.latin: 43:5 Tu es ipse Rex meus et Deus meus: * qui mandas salútes Iacob.
content.english: 43:5 Thou art thyself my king and my God, * who commandest the saving of Jacob.

content.latin: 43:6 In te inimícos nostros ventilábimus cornu: * et in nómine tuo spernémus insurgéntes in nobis.
content.english: 43:6 Through thee we will push down our enemies with the horn: * and through thy name we will despise them that rise up against us.

content.latin: 43:7 Non enim in arcu meo sperábo: * et gládius meus non salvábit me.
content.english: 43:7 For I will not trust in my bow: * neither shall my sword save me.

content.latin: 43:8 Salvásti enim nos de affligéntibus nos: * et odiéntes nos confudísti.
content.english: 43:8 But thou hast saved us from them that afflict us: * and hast put them to shame that hate us.

content.latin: 43:9 In Deo laudábimur tota die: * et in nómine tuo confitébimur in sǽculum.
content.english: 43:9 In God shall we glory all the day long: * and in thy name we will give praise for ever.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: 43:10 Nunc autem repulísti et confudísti nos: * et non egrediéris, Deus, in virtútibus nostris.
content.english: 43:10 But now thou hast cast us off, and put us to shame: * and thou, O God, wilt not go out with our armies.

content.latin: 43:11 Avertísti nos retrórsum post inimícos nostros: * et qui odérunt nos, diripiébant sibi.
content.english: 43:11 Thou hast made us turn our back to our enemies: * and they that hated us plundered for themselves.

content.latin: 43:12 Dedísti nos tamquam oves escárum: * et in géntibus dispersísti nos.
content.english: 43:12 Thou hast given us up like sheep to be eaten: * thou hast scattered us among the nations.

content.latin: 43:13 Vendidísti pópulum tuum sine prétio: * et non fuit multitúdo in commutatiónibus eórum.
content.english: 43:13 Thou hast sold thy people for no price: * and there was no reckoning in the exchange of them.

content.latin: 43:14 Posuísti nos oppróbrium vicínis nostris, * subsannatiónem et derísum his, qui sunt in circúitu nostro.
content.english: 43:14 Thou hast made us a reproach to our neighbours, * a scoff and derision to them that are round about us.

content.latin: 43:15 Posuísti nos in similitúdinem géntibus: * commotiónem cápitis in pópulis.
content.english: 43:15 Thou hast made us a byword among the Gentiles: * a shaking of the head among the people.

content.latin: 43:16 Tota die verecúndia mea contra me est, * et confúsio faciéi meæ coopéruit me.
content.english: 43:16 All the day long my shame is before me: * and the confusion of my face hath covered me.

content.latin: 43:17 A voce exprobrántis, et obloquéntis: * a fácie inimíci, et persequéntis.
content.english: 43:17 At the voice of him that reproacheth and detracteth me: * at the face of the enemy and persecutor.

content.latin: 43:18 Hæc ómnia venérunt super nos, nec oblíti sumus te: * et iníque non égimus in testaménto tuo.
content.english: 43:18 All these things have come upon us, yet we have not forgotten thee: * and we have not done wickedly in thy covenant.

content.latin: 43:19 Et non recéssit retro cor nostrum: * et declinásti sémitas nostras a via tua:
content.english: 43:19 And our heart hath not turned back: * neither hast thou turned aside our steps from thy way.

content.latin: 43:20 Quóniam humiliásti nos in loco afflictiónis, * et coopéruit nos umbra mortis.
content.english: 43:20 For thou hast humbled us in the place of affliction: * and the shadow of death hath covered us.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: 43:21 Si oblíti sumus nomen Dei nostri, * et si expándimus manus nostras ad deum aliénum:
content.english: 43:21 If we have forgotten the name of our God, * and if we have spread forth our hands to a strange god:

content.latin: 43:22 Nonne Deus requíret ista? * ipse enim novit abscóndita cordis.
content.english: 43:22 Shall not God search out these things: * for he knoweth the secrets of the heart.

content.latin: 43:22 Quóniam propter te mortificámur tota die: * æstimáti sumus sicut oves occisiónis.
content.english: 43:22 Because for thy sake we are killed all the day long: * we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.

content.latin: 43:23 Exsúrge, quare obdórmis, Dómine? * exsúrge, et ne repéllas in finem.
content.english: 43:23 Arise, why sleepest thou, O Lord? * arise, and cast us not off to the end.

content.latin: 43:24 Quare fáciem tuam avértis, * oblivísceris inópiæ nostræ, et tribulatiónis nostræ?
content.english: 43:24 Why turnest thou thy face away? * and forgettest our want and our trouble?

content.latin: 43:25 Quóniam humiliáta est in púlvere ánima nostra: * conglutinátus est in terra venter noster.
content.english: 43:25 For our soul is humbled down to the dust: * our belly cleaveth to the earth.

content.latin: 43:26 Exsúrge, Dómine, ádiuva nos: * et rédime nos propter nomen tuum.

content.latin: 109:1 Dixit Dóminus Dómino meo: * Sede a dextris meis:
content.english: 109:1 The Lord said to my Lord: * Sit thou at my right hand:

content.latin: 109:1 Donec ponam inimícos tuos, * scabéllum pedum tuórum.
content.english: 109:1 Until I make thy enemies * thy footstool.

content.latin: 109:2 Virgam virtútis tuæ emíttet Dóminus ex Sion: * domináre in médio inimicórum tuórum.
content.english: 109:2 The Lord will send forth the sceptre of thy power out of Sion: * rule thou in the midst of thy enemies.

content.latin: 109:3 Tecum princípium in die virtútis tuæ in splendóribus sanctórum: * ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.
content.english: 109:3 With thee is the principality in the day of thy strength: in the brightness of the saints: * from the womb before the day star I begot thee.

content.latin: 109:4 Iurávit Dóminus, et non pœnitébit eum: * Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum secúndum órdinem Melchísedech.
content.english: 109:4 The Lord hath sworn, and he will not repent: * Thou art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech.

content.latin: 109:5 Dóminus a dextris tuis, * confrégit in die iræ suæ reges.
content.english: 109:5 The Lord at thy right hand * hath broken kings in the day of his wrath.

content.latin: 109:6 Iudicábit in natiónibus, implébit ruínas: * conquassábit cápita in terra multórum.
content.english: 109:6 He shall judge among nations, he shall fill ruins: * he shall crush the heads in the land of many.

content.latin: 109:7 De torrénte in via bibet: * proptérea exaltábit caput.
content.english: 109:7 He shall drink of the torrent in the way: * therefore shall he lift up the head.

content.latin: 110:1 Confitébor tibi, Dómine, in toto corde meo: * in consílio iustórum, et congregatióne.
content.english: 110:1 I will praise thee, O Lord, with my whole heart; * in the council of the just, and in the congregation.

content.latin: 110:2 Magna ópera Dómini: * exquisíta in omnes voluntátes eius.
content.english: 110:2 Great are the works of the Lord: * sought out according to all his wills.

content.latin: 110:3 Conféssio et magnificéntia opus eius: * et iustítia eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 110:3 His work is praise and magnificence: * and his justice continueth for ever and ever.

content.latin: 110:4 Memóriam fecit mirabílium suórum, miséricors et miserátor Dóminus: * escam dedit timéntibus se.
content.english: 110:4 He hath made a remembrance of his wonderful works, being a merciful and gracious Lord: * he hath given food to them that fear him.

content.latin: 110:5 Memor erit in sǽculum testaménti sui: * virtútem óperum suórum annuntiábit pópulo suo:
content.english: 110:5 He will be mindful for ever of his covenant: * he will shew forth to his people the power of his works.

content.latin: 110:7 Ut det illis hereditátem géntium: * ópera mánuum eius véritas, et iudícium.
content.english: 110:7 That he may give them the inheritance of the Gentiles: * the works of his hands are truth and judgment.

content.latin: 110:8 Fidélia ómnia mandáta eius: confirmáta in sǽculum sǽculi, * facta in veritáte et æquitáte.
content.english: 110:8 All his commandments are faithful: confirmed for ever and ever, * made in truth and equity.

content.latin: 110:9 Redemptiónem misit pópulo suo: * mandávit in ætérnum testaméntum suum.
content.english: 110:9 He hath sent redemption to his people: * he hath commanded his covenant for ever.

content.latin: 110:9 (fit reverentia) Sanctum, et terríbile nomen eius: * inítium sapiéntiæ timor Dómini.
content.english: 110:9 (bow head) Holy and terrible is his name: * the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.

content.latin: 110:10 Intelléctus bonus ómnibus faciéntibus eum: * laudátio eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi.
